Crime And Punishment.meaning: the court decided that the person did commit the crime

Crime And Punishment.meaning: to find an offender guilty and to punish them

Crime And Punishment.meaning: people who obey and respect the law

Crime And Punishment.meaning: punishment by death

Crime And Punishment.meaning: to put cameras in a place where a crime is likely to be committed

Crime And Punishment.meaning: to punish people who do something illegal

The Environment.meaning: to dispose of waste products from chemical processes.

The Environment.meaning: a substance or chemical that can be changed to a natural harmless state by the action of bacteria

The Environment.meaning: to reduce the amount of gases sent out into the air

The Environment.meaning: behavior or products that do not harm the environment

The Environment.meaning: all the organisations concerned with the protection of the environment

Government.meaning: government organizations acting at a national level or within a smaller, local area

Government.meaning: a charity or association that is independent of government or business

Government.meaning: to take part in a series of activities in order to achieve a specific aim.

Government.meaning: the act of providing financial support by the government

Government.meaning: a policy or action adopted for a short time until some more permanent solution is found

Sport And Exercise.collocation: to take up sport/to take up exercise

Sport And Exercise.meaning: to stay in good physical condition

Sport And Exercise.collocation: to place too much value on sport
Sport And Exercise.meaning: to regard sport as too important
Sport And Exercise.example: I would argue that schools place too much value on sport in the curriculum, and participation in sport should be an out-of-school activity.

Sport And Exercise.meaning: a person who takes a keen interest in sport
Sport And Exercise.example: While I think that it is healthy to be a sports fan, people should remember that for most people, sport is just entertainment, not a matter of life and death.

Sport And Exercise.meaning: to achieve the best result ever achieved in a sport
Sport And Exercise.example: Real Madrid have set a record for the number of goals scored in a match.

Sport And Exercise.meaning: the activity of reporting news related to sport
Sport And Exercise.example: Many top sports stars are now known to millions of people around the world because of global sports coverage by the media.

Sport And Exercise.meaning: people who are experts on sport and talk or write about it in the media
Sport And Exercise.example: Not only sports stars, but even some sports commentators have become well- known celebrities.

Sport And Exercise.meaning: the activity of selling products connected with a sport or sportsperson
Sport And Exercise.example: Sports merchandising is a multi-billion dollar business worldwide, in the form of t-shirts and sports equipment.

Sport And Exercise.meaning: an advertising statement, usually by a famous sportsperson, saying that they use or like a particular product.
Sport And Exercise.example: In addition to their fabulous salaries, sports celebrities also make a great deal of money through their endorsement of sporting goods such as trainers or even casual clothes or deodorants! Source of vocabulary: IELTS Ngoc Bach

Space Exploration.meaning: competition between the US and the Soviet Union in the 1950s and 60s to be the first to explore space
Space Exploration.example: The space race in the 1950s marks an important point in the development of space exploration

Space Exploration.meaning: a type of space craft that does not have a person inside
Space Exploration.example: Space probes can be sent to far distances for long periods of time to gather information about different areas in space.

Space Exploration.meaning: a small craft used for travelling between the moon and the larger space craft orbiting the moon.
Space Exploration.example: When the first men walked on the moon they came out of the lunar module. The first man to walk on the moon said "One small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind."

Space Exploration.meaning: To send something into space, following a curved path of a planet or an object as it moves around a star, a moon or a planet
Space Exploration.example: A new satellite has been put into orbit around the earth.

Space Exploration.meaning: a voyage into space which has a person to control it
Space Exploration.example: As manned space flights are so dangerous, many checks must be carried out first.

Space Exploration.meaning: to send a rocket into space
Space Exploration.example: Nowadays, men launch space rockets – not ships – to discover new worlds.

Space Exploration.meaning: the universe, especially when it is thought of as an ordered system
Space Exploration.example: Although the challenge of exploring and understanding the cosmos is exciting, it is also very expensive

Space Exploration.collocation: To pour money into space research
Space Exploration.meaning: to spend enormous amounts of money on space research
Space Exploration.example: Some people argue that it is wasteful to pour money into space research.

Space Exploration.meaning: a flight during which a space craft or part of its equipment is tested
Space Exploration.example: Test flights add to the huge costs of space exploration.

Space Exploration.meaning: a spacecraft designed to be used, for example, to travel between the earth and a space station
Space Exploration.example: The first space shuttle was front-page news, but now people are no longer excited by the concept.

Space Exploration.meaning: a large structure that is sent into space and remains above the earth as a base for people working and travelling in space
Space Exploration.example: Even maintaining an international space station is so expensive that the costs must be shared by several countries.

Space Exploration.meaning: journeys into space
Space Exploration.example: Public interest in the early space voyages was unprecedented.

Space Exploration.meaning: travelling to space as a form of vacation/holiday
Space Exploration.example: Billionaires are the only people who are likely to experience space tourism in the foreseeable future.

Space Exploration.collocation: To discover the mysteries of the universe
Space Exploration.meaning: to find out more about space
Space Exploration.example: Space exploration is an essential element in our attempt to discover the mysteries of the universe.

Space Exploration.meaning: the act of gaining control over the difficult task of exploring space
Space Exploration.example: The conquest of space is a challenge that continues to inspire the public imagination.

Space Exploration.meaning: to make somebody excited about something, especially thinking of the future
Space Exploration.example: The images of the first men on the moon were an inspiration to people, and made them more hopeful about the future.

Space Exploration.meaning: the clothing worn by astronauts.
Space Exploration.example: Astronauts must find it difficult to carry out maintenance tasks during space flights wearing uncomfortable spacesuits and helmets.

Space Exploration.meaning: a space that is completely empty of all substances, including all air or other gas
Space Exploration.example: During manned space flights, astronauts have to live off vacuum-packed food.

Space Exploration.meaning: to experience and deal with conditions that are unpleasant
Space Exploration.example: I doubt that space tourism will have mass appeal in the future. Travellers would have to endure hardships and discomforts such as weightless conditions, vacuum- packed food and wearing spacesuits and helmets.

Space Exploration.meaning: to move slowly in the air
Space Exploration.example: Space tourism would be really boring, simply floating through space and looking out of the window of the spacecraft.

Space Exploration.meaning: the technology of sending electronic devices into space for communications purposes
Space Exploration.example: Satellite technology has resulted in huge advances in communications and information-gathering.

Space Exploration.meaning: a useful result of an activity that was designed to produce something different Explanation: Space programs have produced spin-offs that have revolutionized modern life, such as satellite television and communications. 26. To make space travel commercially viable Meaning: to make space travel a success financially
Space Exploration.example: Holidays in space are just fantasy. It is doubtful if it will ever be possible to make space travel commercially viable.

Space Exploration.collocation: The quest for a new homeland
Space Exploration.meaning: the search for a new place to inhabit
Space Exploration.example: As humans are destroying their own planet, the quest for a new homeland in the universe is essential.

Space Exploration.meaning: creatures from another world
Space Exploration.example: One of the most exciting possibilities of the space program is finding alien life forms on other planets.

Space Exploration.meaning: life that may exist on another planet
Space Exploration.example: The quest for extraterrestrial life will prove that humans are not alone in the universe.

Space Exploration.collocation: In the realm of science fiction
Space Exploration.meaning: only possible in science fiction stories, only fantasy
Space Exploration.example: Most of the arguments in favour of space programs are in the realm of science fiction.
